items.raw_excerpt: It’s 89 years since teenager Ted Wright and his brother Christopher were standing by a reed pond on Humber Estuary’s foreshore at North Ferriby and spotted several large oak planks protruding from the mud.
items.summary_en: Eighty-nine years ago, teenager Ted Wright and his brother Christopher discovered large oak planks sticking out of the mud at North Ferriby on the Humber Estuary. The wooden planks turned out to be Bronze Age boats that had been hidden in the riverbed for thousands of years. The village of North Ferriby is now known for one of Britain's most important archaeological finds.
items.summary_ko: 89년 전, 십대 소년 Ted Wright와 그의 형 Christopher가 험버 강가의 North Ferriby에서 진흙 속에 묻힌 거대한 참나무 판자를 발견했습니다. 그 나무 판자는 수천 년 동안 강 바닥에 숨겨져 있던 청동기 시대 배로 밝혀졌습니다. North Ferriby 마을은 이제 영국에서 가장 중요한 고고학적 발견 중 하나로 알려져 있습니다.
items.title_en: North Ferriby: The Yorkshire village which hid Bronze Age boats for thousands of years
items.title_ko: North Ferriby: 수천 년 동안 청동기 배를 숨겨둔 요크셔 마을
items.title_original: North Ferriby: The Yorkshire village which hid Bronze Age boats for thousands of years - Yorkshire Post

items.raw_excerpt: In an exclusive interview with The Local, experts from 'Faire Integration' discuss Germany’s free and multilingual service to help foreign workers understand their rights – and stop problems at work from spiralling out of control.
items.summary_en: Faire Integration is a free and multilingual service in Germany that helps foreign workers understand their workplace rights. The service offers advice to stop problems at work from getting worse. Foreign workers can use it to learn about their rights in their own language.

items.title_en: Free help for foreign workers in Germany to understand their rights

items.title_original: 'Faire Integration': Where foreign workers in Germany can get free workplace advice

items.raw_excerpt: Figures show the number of under-18s on company payrolls is at its lowest level for five years.
items.summary_en: An 18-year-old bar worker in Herne Bay, Kent says building confidence and skills through work is valuable. HMRC figures show the number of under-18s on company payrolls in the southeast has dropped by nearly 19% since 2024, raising concerns about lost opportunities. The story highlights local teenagers who gained life skills from early work experience.

items.raw_excerpt: Did you ever wonder why people in early photographs rarely smiled? The answer to that question is part of a new experience called 'Don't Smile' opening this Saturday at the Woodstock Museum.
